messages:
maria: Observed a sustained NVMe p99 latency ramp starting ~03:10 UTC right after our nightly batch window. GPU node launches delayed ~30-90s. Anyone else seeing this?

kevin: saw similar in eu-west2. p50 fine, p95->p99 jumps from 4ms -> 40-120ms over ~15m. Could be scrub overlap with end-of-batch IO.

maria: attaching quick iostat and `nvme-cli` stats snippet:
```
Device         r/s    w/s   rkB/s  wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await  r_await w_await svctm  %util
nvme0n1      2100  48000  102400 245760  10.2    2.45   12.4   2.4    12.3    1.0  96.3
```
Also saw increases in `avgqu-sz` and sustained write bursts from `janitor-cleaner` tasks.

sam: ops-bot had an alert earlier, linking it:
ops-bot: "ALERT storage-high-io: nvme0n1 avgqu-sz > 1.5 for 10m on gnode-1134"

kevin: can you check scrub/trim jobs schedule? if scrubs kick at batch end, they will contend w/ tail writes. maybe reduce concurrency or stagger.

maria: scrub schedule shows overlap: nightly batch finishes ~03:05, scrub run scheduled 03:00. Oops.

javier: thoughts on quick mitigations? throttling janitor or moving scrub to later window?

sam: mitigation plan:
- throttle janitor to 20% concurrency on affected pools (rolling)
- bump scrub window to 05:00 for next 24h
- add a temporary placement rule to avoid scheduling new GPU provisioning on nodes with avgqu-sz > 1.0

kevin: agree. I'm pushing a canary to throttle janitor now. monitor for drop in p99.

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-20T03:25:12Z: janitor-throttle=canary -> applied to pool=eu-west2-scratch

maria: after throttle p99 dropped from ~100ms -> ~15-20ms on canaries. GPU launch latency back to normal on those nodes. :thumbsup:

sam: next steps: ticket, follow-up RCA, and permanent schedule change. I'll file the ticket and add ops playbook.

maria: filing ticket now. thanks all.

kevin: +1 on playbook. Also suggest adding a metric alert on `janitor.concurrent_tasks` per-pool to catch this earlier.

javier: will add to backlog.

maria: closing loop: rolling throttle applied account-wide for 2h, scrub rescheduled.

sam: postmortem? low-l severity, operational process gap (schedule overlap). we can close after RCA.

maria: lnks: internal runbook https://redwood.internal/runbooks/storage-scrub and grafana dashboard https://grafana.redwood.net/d/ssd-io

kevin: nice work. keep monitoring.
